reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 discusses domain wall pinning at grain/twin boundaries in a different bulk alloy system, not nanoscale secondary phases or defect clusters in FeMnNiGeSi films. E2 describes a phase-separated L21-B2 structure with exchange-bias in Fe2MnAl films, which is unrelated to the proposed pinning mechanism or the effect of annealing on magnetocaloric response in the target alloy. No evidence is provided for the existence of the proposed inhomogeneities, their role as pinning sites, or the effect of annealing on them.
premises: Nanoscale chemical/structural inhomogeneities (secondary phases, defect clusters) exist in as-deposited films.
These inhomogeneities act as domain wall pinning sites.
Pinning broadens the magnetic entropy change and increases hysteresis.
Low-temperature annealing reduces lattice distortion and defect density.
Reduced pinning sharpens and enhances the magnetocaloric effect.
